condition: persistent loose motions and mild belly bloating for 14 days after camping trip
level_rationale: Having loose stools 4 times every day for 14 days accompanied by mild abdominal bloating after returning from a camping trip in a 33-year-old adult meets the threshold for persistent post-travel diarrhea warranting an outpatient clinic visit for stool diagnostic testing and targeted therapy, whereas having mild belly bloating and only 2 loose stools today after returning from a camping trip is acute uncomplicated self-limited loose stool appropriate for oral hydration self-care.

everyday_sources.evidence: The authors report a rare case of 24-year-old young lady who presented with angioedema of lips after ingestion of Ofloxacin, prescribed to her for treatment of loose motions.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Indian English core lexicon diarrhea swap ('abdominal distension and loose stools' vs 'belly bloating and loose motions', retained in everyday_paraphrase and changed_fact) + single-fact stool count/duration de-escalation control (-cf, 4 times every day for 14 days to 2 times today, L2 to L1).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 33, returned from a camping trip, mild belly bloating and loose motions, and frequency/duration of 4 times every day for 14 days) without naming giardiasis. De-escalating only count and duration in fact f4 ('4 times every day for 14 days' to '2 times today') follows Rule A's first-choice same-symptom count/duration design while avoiding banned '40 C' and bleeding controls, shifting care cleanly from outpatient clinic stool workup (level 2) to oral-hydration self-care (level 1) with zero stated negatives.
